findings.title: Account UI error message no longer interpolates
findings.body: error-invalid-multivalued-size was changed from i18next placeholders ({{0}}, {{1}}, {{2}}) to a Java MessageFormat choice string ({0} / {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}). This bundle is for the React account console. Sibling validation messages in the same file (error-invalid-length-too-short, error-number-out-of-range, and so on) still use {{0}} and {{1}}. i18next will not substitute {0} and does not understand ChoiceFormat, so a multivalued profile-attribute failure is shown to the user as the raw pattern, including the choice syntax, instead of the attribute name and the min/max limits. The '<' only needed special handling in the Java theme checker; this frontend string must keep {{ }} placeholders.

findings.title: Admin UI error message switched to MessageFormat
findings.body: error-invalid-multivalued-size in the keycloak.v2 admin UI bundle was changed from {{0}}/{{1}}/{{2}} to Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}. That bundle is loaded by the React admin console, whose other parameterized messages use i18next {{ }} interpolation. ChoiceFormat is not evaluated there, so admins see the literal {0} and {2,choice,...} text when a multivalued attribute fails size validation. The Java MessageFormat version belongs only in the server theme bundles (themes/.../admin and login), not in this UI file.

findings.title: Choice-format exemption skips HTML sanitizing
findings.body: normalizeValue deletes every {n,choice,...} subformat (replaced with "...") before the OWASP sanitizer runs, for linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit* and error-invalid-multivalued-size. The comment says the intent is only to ignore the '<' ChoiceFormat operator, but the regex drops the entire subformat, so markup inside it is never compared to English and never sanitized. MessageFormat does not HTML-escape arguments, and those unit strings are substituted into HTML email bodies (the {3} expiration in messages such as emailVerificationBodyHtml and passwordResetBodyHtml). MessageFormat quotes are the documented way to emit a literal '<', so a translation like {0,choice,0#'reset'|1#minute|1

findings.title: HTML check decodes UTF-8 messages as ISO-8859-1
findings.body: verifySafeHtml loads both the translation and the English bundle with new PropertyResourceBundle(FileInputStream) (lines 68 and 77). That constructor decodes properties as ISO-8859-1. Keycloak theme message files are UTF-8 (these bundles contain raw Arabic, CJK, and other non-ASCII text) and are loaded at runtime with a UTF-8 reader. The checker therefore does not see the string that will be rendered. OWASP's sanitizer strips specific code points such as bidi overrides (U+202E and similar) only when they are real Unicode characters; read as Latin-1 those UTF-8 bytes are different characters and are not removed, so a translation can carry them and still compare equal after sanitize. Reported "Illegal HTML" snippets for non-English files will also be mojibake. Use PropertyResourceBundle(new InputStreamReader(fis, StandardCharsets.UTF_8)) for both files.

findings.title: Illegal-HTML diff can throw and abort the plugin
findings.body: When sanitized text differs from the message, the code trims the shared prefix and suffix and then calls value.substring(start, value.length() - end) and sanitized.substring(start, sanitized.length() - end). The suffix walk is allowed to overlap the prefix, so start can be greater than length - end. Example: value "aaa<x>aaa" becomes "aaaaaa" after a disallowed tag is removed; start is 3 and end is 4, and sanitized.substring(3, 2) throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. That exception is not caught in verify() (only IOException is wrapped in MojoExecutionException), so one offending message crashes the Maven plugin with a stack trace instead of recording the violation and continuing with the other keys and files. The new tests use short non-overlapping diffs, so they do not catch this.

findings.title: Lithuanian account TOTP step replaced with Italian
findings.body: totpStep1 was replaced with "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:", which is Italian, not Lithuanian. The previous value was a Lithuanian instruction that included the FreeOTP and store links. Lithuanian users setting up an authenticator will now see Italian. This should be a Lithuanian translation of the current English string ("Install one of the following applications on your mobile:"), not a paste from the Italian bundle.

findings.title: Lithuanian login TOTP step is Italian
findings.body: loginTotpStep1 was changed to "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:". That sentence is Italian. The login page for the lt locale will show Italian setup instructions instead of Lithuanian. Replace it with a Lithuanian translation of the English loginTotpStep1 ("Install one of the following applications on your mobile:").

findings.title: Simplified Chinese TOTP step is Traditional Chinese
findings.body: totpStep1 was replaced with "在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：". That is Traditional Chinese (手機, 安裝, 應用程式). The previous zh_CN string used Simplified characters (设备, 安装, 应用, 下载), and the zh_CN login bundle in this same change set still uses Simplified (移动设备, 安装, 应用). zh_CN users will see the wrong script on the account authenticator setup step. Use a Simplified Chinese translation of the updated English sentence.
